sources.text: Too tight even for NYC - Review of Blue Note, New York City, NY - Tripadvisor But hey, it's about the MUSiC so ... you go upstairs and chat with jazz greats after the show as we did. Intimate venue and crowded but totally worth it.... As many others have said, don't go hear expecting fine dining and order 2 drinks when you sit down as it's tough for servers to even reach you. But hey, it's about the MUSiC so enjoy it, have a drink or two but don't nitpick the food or the somewhat rude service. Where else can you go upstairs and chat with jazz greats after the show as we did. Intimate venue and crowded but totally worth it. Probably one of my least favorite jazz venues. Packed at long tables, you could be the one at the far end. Servers are friendly, food descent but very slow to come. Show we went to was very sad, McCoy Tyner wasn't in condition to play, just embarassing that a jazz great was pushed onto the stage, literally.. This famed New York venue, in the heart of Greenwich Village, has been featuring many of the jazz world’s greats since it opened in 1981. I myself was there to see the wonderful Cassandra Wilson perform an all too brief one hour set which left me wanting more. Much more. Unfortunately, Wilson was performing two separate sets a night (over four nights), so her time on stage was severely restricted. This is worth bearing in mind if you are planning to visit the venue.
